evidence.supports: County's own agenda packet shows Ordinance 2026-037 as a third-reading item imposing a moratorium on data-center development applications.
evidence.quote: 2026-037: An Ordinance imposing a moratorium on the acceptance, processing, or approval of development applications for data centers and all other land use or development approvals for data centers; and other matters related thereto.

evidence.supports: Confirms passage of the third and final reading on Aug. 18, 2026 (Tuesday), a six-month term.
evidence.quote: Anderson County Council passed a six-month moratorium on data centers Tuesday night. County administrator Rusty Burns confirmed that council passed the third and final reading of the moratorium.

decisions.notes: Primary county agenda plus news confirmation. Temporary six-month pause. No duplicate elsewhere in SC. Not an OLDER item.

evidence.supports: Confirms unanimous third and final reading on Sept. 14, 2026, preceded by a public hearing.
evidence.quote: The Clarendon County Council passed its third and final reading for a moratorium pausing future data center development in the county. The moratorium was unanimously passed with no one opposed.

evidence.supports: Names the ordinance (2026-18), its scope (data centers and battery storage outside Industrial I/II zones), the Project 59 carve-out, and the Aug. 24 second reading leading to the Sept. 14 third reading.
evidence.quote: Council unanimously gave second reading to Ordinance 2026-18 during a special called meeting. A public hearing is expected before third and final reading at council's Sept. 14 regular meeting.

decisions.notes: Two independent local/regional news sources agree on the ordinance number, scope, and Sept. 14, 2026 final-reading date. A September-dated Island Packet statewide roundup (also cited in the Sumter County item below) separately lists Clarendon as still 'Proposed,' but that roundup appears to predate or simply lag the county-specific reporting cited here, which is more specific (ordinance number, vote detail, two independent outlets); treated as confirmed. Temporary pause with a carve-out for an already-approved project, not a permanent ban. No duplicate elsewhere in SC.

evidence.supports: Full primary ordinance text declaring a 12-month temporary moratorium on data centers in Fairfield County.
evidence.quote: AN ORDINANCE AUTHORIZING FAIRFIELD COUNTY COUNCIL TO DECLARE A TWELVE MONTH TEMPORARY MORATORIUM ON DATA CENTERS IN FAIRFIELD COUNTY, SOUTH CAROLINA, TO INVOKE THE PENDING ORDINANCE DOCTRINE

evidence.supports: Confirms the moratorium and its comprehensive-study requirement.
evidence.quote: In Fairfield County, which granted initial approval to a 12-month moratorium in August, are planning to research data centers over the next year through town halls, work sessions with experts and visits to existing facilities.

decisions.notes: Primary ordinance text plus news corroboration. Temporary 12-month pause invoking the pending-ordinance doctrine, not a permanent ban. No duplicate elsewhere in SC.

evidence.supports: Reports the unanimous third and final reading (with one member voting remotely), a one-year term, and that the first and second readings passed Aug. 25 and Sept. 8, 2026.
evidence.quote: Kershaw County Council voted to pass a third and final reading of an ordinance establishing a temporary moratorium on data centers, cryptocurrency mining operations and data processing facilities. ... The first and second readings were passed on Aug. 25 and Sept 8, respectively.

evidence.supports: Independently confirms the Aug. 25 first reading and Sept. 8 unanimous second reading and the ordinance's scope and pending-ordinance-doctrine trigger.
evidence.quote: Kershaw County Council unanimously approved the second reading of a proposed 12-month moratorium on data centers Tuesday, Sept. 8, giving county officials more time to study the rapidly growing industry and develop local regulations.

decisions.notes: Two independent sources, consistent reading-by-reading timeline culminating in the Sept. 22, 2026 third reading. Temporary pause tied to a study period, not a permanent ban. No duplicate elsewhere in SC.

evidence.supports: Reports the 6-0 third-reading vote Sept. 14, 2026 (Monday), and sponsor Vice Chairman Matthew Brownlee's stated purpose.
evidence.quote: Laurens County Council voted on Monday to approve a one-year pause on data centers. The council unanimously approved the third and final reading of the moratorium with a vote of six to zero.

evidence.supports: Independently corroborates the 6-0 vote and one-year term, applying to unincorporated areas.
evidence.quote: Laurens County Council voted 6-0 Monday night to approve a one-year moratorium on new data center development in the county's unincorporated areas.

decisions.notes: Two independent local outlets agree on vote count, date, and scope (unincorporated county only, cities retain their own control). Temporary pause, not a permanent ban. No duplicate elsewhere in SC.

evidence.supports: County's own agenda shows the moratorium ordinance at third reading and public hearing on Sept. 8, 2026, with its full title.
evidence.quote: An Ordinance Declaring a Temporary Moratorium on the Acceptance of, Review of, and/or Action Upon Applications for Rezoning, Special Exceptions, Special Use Permits, Building Permits, Site Plans, Plan of Development for Siting, Economic Incentives, Fee in Lieu of Taxes or Any Other Form of Incentive, That Would Authorize or Permit the Development or Construction of Data Centers, Data Processing Facilities, Cryptocurrency Mining Operations or Any Other Uses Associated with Data Processing Facilities Within Orangeburg County

evidence.supports: Confirms the moratorium was approved, giving county leaders time to study appropriate rules.
evidence.quote: Orangeburg County Council approved a moratorium on new data center development, giving leaders time to study what rules should apply.

decisions.notes: Primary county agenda for the third-reading/public-hearing date plus news confirmation of passage. A September-dated Island Packet statewide roundup separately lists Orangeburg as 'Proposed,' but that roundup is undated within the archived text and its own internal list (e.g., listing Colleton as 'Adopted July 6' while this inventory already has Colleton as replaced/superseded) suggests it is a point-in-time snapshot that may predate the Sept. 8 vote confirmed here by two independent primary/news sources; treated as confirmed. Temporary pause, not a permanent ban. No duplicate elsewhere in SC.

evidence.supports: Reports the Sept. 21, 2026 final-reading vote and the amendments defining the 65 MW threshold and industrial-site exemption.
evidence.quote: County Council has given final approval to a moratorium on new data centers, but that 12-month pause won't apply to facilities smaller than 65 megawatts and many that want to set up on industrial sites.

evidence.supports: Independently corroborates the 5-1 vote and the amendment conditions.
evidence.quote: Spartanburg County Council voted 5-1 Monday night to approve a one-year freeze on new data centers, adopting several key amendments that define what facilities can still move forward.

decisions.notes: Two independent regional outlets agree on the vote (5-1), date (Sept. 21, 2026), and the amended scope (65 MW threshold, industrial-site carve-out, Valara exclusion). Temporary pause with conditional exemptions, not a blanket permanent ban. No duplicate elsewhere in SC.
